newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt '98 real wage rise target of 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt '98 real wage rise target of 1.5 pct.

text.p: The Hungarian government said on Thursday it was targeting a 14.5 percent private sector wage rise in 1998, or 1.5 percent above projected inflation.
"The government's main target is to keep wage increases in line with the main macroeconomic figures," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following a cabinet meeting.
He said Hungary is expected to have 3.5 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1998 and average inflation of 13 percent.

In the first four months of 1997 wages in the business sector grew by 23 percent over the same period of 1996, while public sector wages grew by 31.8 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period of 1996.
This compares to an 18.6 percent year on year consumer price inflation in April.
Kiss added that the government expects overall wages to grow by an average 20 percent this year.

A statement added that the government plans to immediately start negotiations with private employers' and employees' representatives over the proposed 14.5 percent average wage rise, setting a ceiling of 16 percent for the best performers.
Kiss could not say what the 1998 wage hike target was for the public sector but said the starting point would be the same.
